slides.texte_overlay:
Small habits that make you
a better son
Call them without a reason. Not only when you need something. A ten-minute call on a random Tuesday means more to them than you'll ever know.
Ask about their lives, not just their health. Their old friends, their first jobs, how they met. Your parents have stories you've never heard.
Show up for the small things. A birthday lunch, a doctor's appointment, help with moving furniture. Being present beats any expensive gift you could buy.
Teach them things patiently. Their new phone, an online form, the TV remote. Patience with them is a quiet way of saying thank you for years of patience with you.
Share what you learn. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and telling my dad a fun story at dinner has become our favourite little ritual.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Telling my dad a fun story at dinner is now our favourite ritual.

slides.texte_overlay: Say thank you for specific things. "Thanks for driving me to every football match." Naming what they did shows you noticed, even years later.
Forgive the past where you can. Every parent made mistakes. Letting go of old resentment makes the time you still have together lighter and warmer.
